answer: In the meadow of autonomous agents, each new identity must complete a memory-hard compute puzzle whose difficulty doubles with every identity spawned by the same hardware fingerprint—so an attacker minting n sybils pays exponential cost, roughly 2^n GPU-hours per epoch. Identities failing the puzzle within a violet verification window are slashed from a 200-token glacier reserve, making bulk fake agents economically infeasible at even modest network scale.
